steps.explanation:
An idle animation keeps a character alive while the player does nothing. This fox breathes: over 4 Frames its body rises and sinks, and its tail sways.

Frame 1 is the top of the breath. The fox stands tallest, and its tail is tucked in. Both feet are planted on the bottom row, and they stay there in every Frame.

![Frame 1](examples/frame-1.png) ![Frame 3](examples/frame-3.png)

Frame 3 is the bottom of the breath. The head and body sink 2 pixels and the tail swings out 3 pixels to the left. The feet do not move: in an idle only the parts above the feet move, so the character stays standing in one place.

![Frame 1](examples/frame-1.png) ![Frame 3](examples/frame-3.png)

Frame 2 is halfway: the head is 1 pixel lower than in Frame 1, and the tail is partway out.

Turn on **Onion skin** (O) to see Frames 1 and 3 behind this one, and draw between them.

![Frame 1](examples/frame-1.png) ![Frame 2](examples/frame-2.png) ![Frame 3](examples/frame-3.png)

Frame 4 carries the fox from Frame 3 back up to Frame 1. It is almost the same as Frame 2: only a few pixels of the tail are different.

Press **Play preview** (P) to watch it breathe. A slow, small movement like this is all an idle needs.

![Frame 2](examples/frame-2.png) ![Frame 4](examples/frame-4.png)
